newsitem.title: CROATIA: SOCCER-CROATIA CALL UP TWO NEWCOMERS FOR DENMARK TIE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CROATIA CALL UP TWO NEWCOMERS FOR DENMARK TIE.

text.p: Croatian coach Miroslav Blazevic called up two new players in his 20-man squad for next Saturday's World Cup qualifier against Denmark in Split, Croatian media reported on Monday.
Defender Niko Kovac of German first division Bayer Leverkusen and midfielder Nenad Pralija of Spain's Espanyol are the new names for last year's European championship quarter-finalists.
Croatia beat Denmark 3-0 in Euro 96 in a memorable match before going out 2-1 to eventual champions Germany in quarter-finals.

Croatia rely heavily on their experienced "foreign legion", including strikers Davor Suker of Real Madrid and Alen Boksic of Juventus, AC Milan midfielder Zvonimir Boban and Real Betis defender Robert Jarni.

After managing only a 1-1 draw against Greece in Zagreb, Croatia need all six points from two key games in Split -- against Denmark on Saturday and against Slovenia four days later -- in order to qualify for the 1998 World Cup finals in France from a relatively weak group.

"The most important thing is that all the players I was counting on will come to Split. This concerns especially Suker, who has managed to recover from injury," the Zagreb daily Vjesnik quoted Blazevic as saying.
"This game is our 'to be or not to be'."
Goalkeepers - Drazen Ladic (Croatia Zagreb), Tonci Gabric (Hajduk Split), Marijan Mrmic (Besiktas Istanbul, Turkey)

Defenders - Niko Kovac (Bayer Leverkusen, Germany), Slaven Bilic (West Ham, England), Nikola Jerkan (Nottingham Forest, England), Igor Stimac (Derby County, England), Dario Simic (Croatia), Robert Jarni (Real Betis, Spain)

Midfielders - Zvonimir Soldo (VfB Stuttgart, Germany), Mario Stanic (Parma, Italy), Robert Prosinecki (Sevilla, Spain), Nikola Jurcevic (Freiburg, Germany), Zvonimir Boban (AC Milan, Italy), Aljosa Asanovic (Derby County, England), Nenad Pralija (Espanyol, Spain)
Strikers - Alen Boksic (Juventus, Italy), Davor Suker (Real Madrid, Spain), Goran Vlaovic (Valencia, Spain), Igor Cvitanovic (Croatia).
